glosses: Frapper, blesser ou tuer avec un poignard.

examples.text: Nous avons dit ailleurs que la place sur laquelle existait l'ancien Opéra devait recevoir un monument expiatoire pour le Duc de Berry, poignardé par Louvel, au sortir du spectacle ; […].
Pareille à la Mallonia déshonorée par Tibère et se présentant devant le sénat romain pour accuser son violateur, avant de se poignarder en son désespoir, Henriette entra dans la salle des austères.

glosses: Causer une extrême douleur, une extrême affliction.

examples.text: Il ne faut pas lui faire ce reproche ; ce serait le poignarder.

glosses: An act of stabbing or thrusting with an object.

examples.text: A knife was flashing in his hand, and just as he was about to take a stab at me, the smith grabbed his arm from behind.

glosses: A wound made by stabbing.

examples.text: I opened the man's linen robe, and there over his heart was a dagger-wound, and beneath the woman's fair breast was a like cruel stab, through which her life had ebbed away.

glosses: Pain inflicted on a person's feelings.

examples.text: “I bet you two have really big plans. And might I say, that is just fab,” he said of Lynn's dress. “I'm glad someone noticed,” she replied, seeming to take a stab at me.

examples.text: a horn stab

glosses: A bacterial culture made by inoculating a solid medium, such as gelatin, with the puncture of a needle or wire.
To pierce or to wound (somebody) with a (usually pointed) tool or weapon, especially a knife or dagger.

examples.text: If you stab him in the heart he won't live long enough to retaliate.

"There the cause of death was soon ascertained ; the victim of this daring outrage had been stabbed to death from ear to ear with a long, sharp instrument, in shape like an antique stiletto, which […] was subsequently found under the cushions of the hansom.[…]"

Hornet blazed away as best she could, but, having to split her attention between high and low attackers, as well as having the aft 5-inch battery temporarily disabled by a young officer who'd accidentally run the guns into their stops, freezing them in position until the issue could be sorted, meant that two 550-pound semi-armor-piercing bombs, and one fractionally-lighter high-explosive bomb, soon crashed down, the first two stabbing deep into the ship and the other one blowing a hole in the flight deck, accompanied by a dive bomber that had been shot down but elected to go out by slamming into the Hornet as opposed to the sea. In some small comfort, that aircraft's bomb didn't go off as well.

glosses: To thrust in a stabbing motion.

examples.text: to stab a dagger into a person

glosses: To recklessly hit with the tip of a (usually pointed) object, such as a weapon or finger (often used with at).

examples.text: He stabbed at my face with the twig but luckily kept missing my eyes.
None shall dare / With shortened sword to stab in closer war.
Towards thee I roll, thou all-destroying but unconquering whale; to the last I grapple with thee; from hell's heart I stab at thee; for hate's sake I spit my last breath at thee.

glosses: To cause a sharp, painful sensation (often used with at).

examples.text: The snow from the blizzard was stabbing at my face as I skied down the mountain.

glosses: To injure secretly or by malicious falsehood or slander.

examples.text: to stab a person's reputation

glosses: To roughen a brick wall with a pick so as to hold plaster.
To pierce folded sheets, near their back edges, for the passage of thread or wire.
To guide the end of a pipe into a coupling when making up a connection.

examples.text: [O]ne of the derrickman's jobs is to "stab" the pipe.

glosses: The horizontal or vertical stabilizer of an aircraft.

examples.text: If the pilots used electric pitch trim, it would only pause MCAS for 5s; to deactivate it you have to switch off the STAB TRIM CUTOUT switches.

glosses: Clipping of established.

examples.text: Do you know whether any country offices pay their men by the thousand, or whether they are on stab wages? — I do not know. Some are paid stab wages, but I do not know whether there is much piece-work.
The pressmen were granted a stab wage of 36s for a 60 hour week, and the extras for overtime and Sunday work […]

glosses: Clipping of establishment.

examples.text: […] there were 286 overseers and 210 readers occupied in the 501 offices; 2,691 compositors were paid on the stab […]

glosses: Herir con un puñal.

examples.text: Su guardaespaldas le apuñaló, matándole, en el año 41.
Vikernes apuñaló 23 veces a Euronymous causándole la muerte.
Un oficial, Manuel Palacios, entró a la casa y apuñaló al exconde.
Una vez en Valladolid, apuñaló en una pendencia a un caballero y tuvo que viajar por varios lugares de España refugiándose de la justicia, hasta que éste sanó y pudo arreglarse el asunto.

colpire a tradimento
doorboren, prikken

examples.text: Hij stak het mes diep in het vlees.
Zijn slangen eigenlijk nachtdieren? Af en toe stak ik mijn hoofd naar buiten, maar ik zag gelukkig niks.

glosses: in brand ~: doen ontvlammen

examples.text: De invallers staken het hele dorp in brand.

glosses: ~ in: investeren

examples.text: Tot slot zijn vaders meer tijd in hun kinderen gaan steken - waardoor kinderen per saldo nog steeds op behoorlijk wat 'oudertijd' kunnen rekenen.

De Chinese auto heeft dus definitief een plek veroverd op de Europese markt. Bovag verwacht dat het marktaandeel van Chinese autofabrikanten van 4 procent nu naar 10 procent zal groeien in Europa en wel 15 procent in Nederland. "De Chinese merken zijn al een serieuze speler en ik denk dat ze Europese fabrikanten gaan stimuleren nog meer te steken in de elektrificering en efficiëntie van hun auto's", zegt Brummelhuis. De EU hoopt in ieder geval binnenkort afspraken te maken China zodat Chinese automerken ook hier meer fabrieken gaan openen.

glosses: iets ergens in doen

examples.text: Ze had zo'n zware, navulbare zilveren aansteker, meer een tafelmodel dan iets wat je in je zak zou steken.
